She was saying something about how she didn't believe in doctors and that my siblings literally beg her to go and she still puts off taking them as long as possible. I told her that's not okay, that she did that to me and I nearly died (I was hospitalized for weeks, and spent several months on bedrest recovering), and that if she keeps that up one of us really might die some day because of her. She didn't take that too well, but ended up dropping it and brushing it off as no big deal. Later on, she asked me to go grab her a drink and when I asked her what she wanted she said "well you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years!" This is the second time today that you've been mean to me and tried to make me seem like a bad person!" I told her I'm not trying to be mean I was just saying it's not cool to not take your kid to the doctor and that I'm not going to know anything about her since I didnt grow up with her. We ended up going home shortly after and went out again the other night, a few weeks later. Well I got my brother a phone because they kept taking his (that a different family member pays for) and I wanted him to have his own, so I made it clear they can keep his other one and this one is STRICTLY for him. Well I found out they've been taking and using this one too, so when I saw her I told her, seriously, I dont want to take the phone back because I don't want him to be punished for what you're doing, but I will take it back if you don't stop stealing it from him. That is HIS that I'M paying for, not you, it is not yours to touch, it's already bad enough that you keep all his work money at least don't touch his phone. She got upset and starting yelling and crying saying I need to stop treating her like a bad mother, and I told her well to be honest she kind of IS one. She had a meltdown and started sobbing and said well fine, I don't need you in my life anyways, and left without me. Now my family is saying I shouldn't of treated her like that even if she wasn't that great to me. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to tell my mom that she's a bad mother. Let me start by understanding the situation better. From what I gather, there were a couple of incidents where I said things to my mom that upset her. The first time was when she was talking about not believing in doctors and how my siblings had to beg her to take them, even though she still put it off. I told her that's not okay because she did the same to me, and I nearly died because of it. I was hospitalized for weeks and had to spend several months on bed rest recovering. I was worried that if she keeps doing that, one of us might die someday because of her actions. She didn't take it well but eventually dropped the subject. Then, later that day, she asked me to grab her a drink and when I asked what she wanted, she said, "Well, you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years!" I responded by saying I don't know what she likes because my grandparents raised me and I still don't know anything about her. She got upset, started crying, and said, "What's your problem? This is the second time today that you've been mean to me and tried to make me seem like a bad person!" I tried to explain that I wasn't trying to be mean, just saying it's not cool not to take the kids to the doctor, and that I don't know anything about her since I didn't grow up with her. We ended up going home shortly after. A few weeks later, we went out again. I had gotten my brother a phone because they kept taking his (which a different family member pays for), and I wanted him to have his own. I made it clear they can keep his other one, and this one is STRICTLY for him. But I found out they've been taking and using this one too. When I saw her, I told her seriously that I don't want to take the phone back because I don't want him to be punished for what she's doing, but I will take it back if she doesn't stop stealing it from him. I explained that it's HIS phone that I'm paying for, not hers, and it's already bad enough that she keeps all his work money, so at least don't touch his phone. She got upset, started yelling and crying, saying I need to stop treating her like a bad mother, and I told her honestly that she kind of IS one. She had a meltdown, started sobbing, and said, "Well fine, I don't need you in my life anyway," and left without me. Now, my family is saying I shouldn't have treated her like that, even if she wasn't that great to me. So, is it right or wrong for me to tell my mom she's a bad mother? First, I need to consider the context of our relationship. It seems like there's a history of her not taking the kids to the doctor, which has had serious consequences for me. That's a significant issue because it's about my health and well-being. I nearly died because of her actions, which is a heavy burden to carry. Then, there's the issue of the phone. She's taking my brother's phone, which I paid for, and using it. That's a violation of boundaries, especially since I made it clear that it's strictly for him. It's one thing if she's borrowing it, but if she's stealing it, that's a different level of disrespect. Additionally, she's keeping my brother's work money. That's another boundary issue. It's his money, and she has no right to keep it. This seems like a pattern of behavior where she's not respecting personal boundaries, whether it's about health, finances, or personal belongings. When I told her she's a bad mother, I was expressing my frustration and hurt. It's understandable that I would feel that way given the circumstances. However, calling her a bad mother is a strong statement. It's important to communicate feelings without being overly judgmental or hurtful. I also need to consider the impact of my words on our relationship. While it's important to set boundaries and express how her actions affect me, using such strong language can escalate the situation and lead to a breakdown in communication. It might be more effective to express my feelings in a way that focuses on the specific behaviors rather than labeling her as a bad mother. Moreover, family dynamics are complex. My family is advising me not to treat her like that, even if she wasn't great to me. They might be concerned about maintaining family harmony or not wanting to escalate conflicts further. It's important to weigh the advice of others against my own feelings and the need to protect my well-being. In the end, it's a balance between expressing my feelings honestly and maintaining respectful communication. It's okay to set boundaries and let her know how her actions affect me, but labeling her as a bad mother might not be the most constructive approach. It's important to communicate in a way that allows for understanding and potential resolution rather than causing further conflict. So, considering all these factors, I think it's not entirely wrong to express frustration and set boundaries, but the way I did it by calling her a bad mother might not be the best approach. It's more about how I communicate my feelings rather than the content of what I'm saying.
